newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher, but rally loses steam.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher, but rally loses steam.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed higher for the fourth consecutive day on Friday, but the rally lost some steam as profit-taking kicked in after recent gains, brokers said.
Wall Street's surge past the 7,000 barrier helped certain global stocks, but the overall impact was limited, they added.

Tokyo's key market index drifted sideways throughout the day, as investors extended their purchases to a wider range of blue-chip issues, while major multinationals were weighed down by profit-taking, brokers said.

"The (recent) rally had been led by high-priced stocks, but today people started to shop for lower-priced issues, such as in the steel sector," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities.
Shares in Nippon Steel Corp jumped in heavy trade, rising 23 yen yen or 7.44 percent to end at 332. The volume of 18.343 million shares was the largest on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE).
"There are expectations of growing profits in the steel industry, and the weak yen will further help its earnings," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities.
Shares in the telecommunications industry jumped in the afternoon, prompted by bargain hunting by foreign investors and
Telecommunications giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp closed 13,000 yen higher at 885,000 yen.
DDI Corp, which offers long-distance telephone services, ended 51,000 yen higher at 749,000 yen.
Japanese semiconductor-related shares gained ground, encouraged by expectations of a recovery in the global chip market, brokers said.
Tokyo Electron Ltd, which makes semiconductor-manufacturing equipment, ended up 140 yen at 4,530 yen, its highest level for this financial year.
Dainippon Screen Manufacturing Co Ltd, which also makes semiconductor-manufacturing equipment, rose in active trade and ended up 10 yen at 1,050 yen.
The second-section index rose 8.79 points to end at 1,737.77, with 9.45 million shares traded. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 6.29 points at 1,235.73.
